title: installer: support air-gapped observability bundle input (local path) + CLI help/docs
author: Bruno Silva
release_notes:
- Private installer: add --observability-bundle / path-based offline install option for dashboards/rules/logging defaults.
- Improve CLI help and operator docs for air-gapped/on-prem workflows.
description:
Summary: This adds support for installing the Private observability minimum pack from a local, air-gapped artifact (directory or .tar.gz) instead of downloading from Redwood-hosted URLs. The installer now accepts a new bundle input path that contains dashboards, PrometheusRule YAML, and logging config defaults, and wires that into the existing apply/provision steps. Also updates CLI help output and docs to reflect the offline flow.

Motivation: On-prem / constrained-egress installs frequently cannot reach our artifact endpoints, and we’ve been doing bespoke “scp the files and manually patch the installer” workflows. This PR standardizes the artifact format and adds first-class flags so Solutions can run consistent installs and upgrades.

What’s included:
- New CLI flag: --observability-bundle (alias: --obs-bundle) pointing to either:
  - a local directory (unpacked bundle), or
  - a local .tar.gz bundle file.
- Bundle format contract (expected layout):
  - dashboards/ (Grafana JSON files + folder provisioning)
  - rules/ (PrometheusRule YAML groups)
  - logging/ (Vector/Fluent Bit default config templates)
  - metadata.json (pack version + optional checksums)
- Installer behavior:
  - If --observability-bundle is set, installer uses it and skips network fetch.
  - If both --observability-bundle and --observability-pack-version are provided, bundle wins and we log a warning (keeps backwards-compatible flags for non-air-gapped installs).
  - Path is validated early with actionable error messages (missing required dirs/files, unreadable tar, etc).
  - Tar extraction occurs into the installer working directory under a temp folder with secure permissions; temp is cleaned up on success and best-effort on failure.
  - Optional checksum verification: if metadata.json includes sha256 entries we verify extracted files.
- Security posture:
  - No new outbound calls.
  - Explicitly prevents bundle path traversal during extraction (rejects entries with .., absolute paths, or symlinks).
  - Does not print file contents or secrets in logs; only logs filenames and counts.
- Docs/help:
  - Updates `redwood-private-installer install --help` output examples.
  - Adds an “Air-gapped observability pack install” section to the operator docs page referenced by the installer.

Out of scope:
- Building the offline bundle itself (handled by the release pipeline / ENG-2846 follow-ups).
- Adding a new logging backend or changing customer SIEM integrations.

Testing:
- Unit tests for bundle detection (dir vs tar), validation errors, and safe extraction.
- Local manual test: on-prem lab cluster with egress disabled; ran `install --observability-bundle ./private-observability-pack-0.3.0.tgz` and confirmed dashboards provision and Prometheus rules load.

Notes for reviewers:
- Please sanity-check the tar extraction guardrails (Marcus).
- Please confirm the bundle layout matches the on-prem packaging notes (Fatima).
- Docs wording is intentionally prescriptive: we need a single supported format to reduce support load (Elliot).

Related:
- ENG-2846 (air-gapped packaging)
- ENG-2847 (validation harness) will later validate the bundle contents post-install.
- SUP-2427 is the customer report that kicked off “offline artifacts” priority.

Screenshots/logs:
- Included in commit 3 as a short install log excerpt (no secrets).

conversation:
Fatima Noor (review) — 2025-02-13: Bundle layout looks good and matches what we’ve been doing manually, but please make `metadata.json` optional for early bundles. Also, for directory bundles, can we allow missing `logging/` if a customer is forwarding logs elsewhere?

Bruno Silva (author) — 2025-02-13: Good call. I made metadata optional (only used for checksums/version display). For `logging/`, I’d prefer it required to keep “supported baseline,” but we can make it optional behind a flag. Let me check with Vivek/Sean whether we consider logging defaults a minimum requirement.

Sean Gallagher — 2025-02-14: For the minimum pack, logging defaults are part of the supported baseline, but customers can disable log shipping. Suggest: keep `logging/` in the bundle contract, but allow `--disable-log-pipeline` to skip applying it.

Bruno Silva (author) — 2025-02-14: Done in latest push: bundle still expects `logging/` but install step can be skipped with `--disable-log-pipeline` (existing flag). Validation now checks presence unless the disable flag is set.

Marcus Lin (review) — 2025-02-14: +1 on no outbound calls. Two security asks: (1) ensure tar extraction rejects symlinks and hardlinks, and (2) ensure we don’t follow symlinks if they exist in the directory bundle.

Bruno Silva (author) — 2025-02-15: Addressed. Tar extraction fails on any link type. For directory bundles, we now `Lstat` and reject symlinks in the bundle tree. Added tests for both.

Elliot Price (review) — 2025-02-16: Docs: can we include a concrete example command and a note about where to copy the bundle on the bastion? Also please clarify precedence when both bundle path and version are provided.

Bruno Silva (author) — 2025-02-16: Updated docs with a copy-to-bastion step and example. Added explicit precedence note in both docs and `--help`.

Sahana Iyer (review) — 2025-02-17: CI: can we add a unit test to ensure extraction cleans up temp dirs on error? We’ve had disk bloat in repeated runs.

Bruno Silva (author) — 2025-02-17: Added `TestExtractCleansUpOnFailure` and switched cleanup to `defer` best-effort with an explicit log on failure.

Connor O'Brien (review) — 2025-02-18: Looks mergeable. Please ensure release notes mention the new flag and that it’s compatible with existing workflows.

Bruno Silva (author) — 2025-02-18: Added release notes in description; no behavior change unless flag is used.
